summary_en: An unsuccessful mayoral candidate filed a "petition" claiming the number of council seats in Nesvady was set wrongly because the town had 4,966 inhabitants on 30 June 2022, below the 5,001 threshold. The court asked him to fix defects in the filing, including the type of action, his standing and a proper petitum. He did not do so, and the court rejected the filing under § 59(3) of the Administrative Court Procedure Code (SSP).

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate, who got 428 votes to the winner's 429, challenged the result. He pointed to the gap between 861 voters who took part and 860 envelopes returned, suggested the 3 invalid ballots might have been misjudged, and claimed the winner's representative disrupted the count. He asked the court to recount. The court found no mismatch between the record and the municipality's published results and called his claims speculative and impossible to verify without redoing the whole count. It rejected the complaint as inadmissible under § 312h(2) SSP without recounting.

A party coalition (SMER-SD and REPUBLIKA) sought to have the 2022 mayoral election in Kysucký Lieskovec declared invalid. Its candidate had not been registered because of a conditional criminal sentence, and it argued that the local electoral commission never properly decided on this. The District Court in Žilina had already upheld the non-registration in a final ruling (7 S 1/2022), and no constitutional complaint had affected that ruling by election day. The court therefore held that the coalition had not filed a valid candidate list and had no standing, and it rejected the complaint by a 5:0 vote. The court added that the later ruling of 14 October 2022, which found the candidate had proved himself during his probation (osvedčil sa), did not change this.

An unsuccessful council candidate asked for a recount of valid votes in electoral district no. 1 of Raková. He argued that a human counting error might have occurred because the count was not checked, and that the margin between the elected and non-elected candidate was only 2 votes. The court found this was a mere speculative assumption with no concrete facts or evidence, and rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP without examining the ballots.

The second-placed mayoral candidate argued that the elected mayor of Bystrany was ineligible because he had convictions for intentional crimes that had not been expunged. The court obtained his criminal record extract. It found that three convictions were expunged only by a district court resolution of 2 December 2022, after the 29 October 2022 election. The mayor was therefore ineligible on election day under § 6(b) of Act 180/2014, and the court declared the mayoral election invalid by a 5:0 vote.

summary_en: The second-placed mayoral candidate in Hucín (145 vs 123 votes) alleged that on election day goods and alcohol were handed out free at a grocery near the polling station in exchange for votes for the winner, breaching the campaign moratorium, and asked the court to obtain CCTV footage. The court found the claims abstract and unsupported: the police records he submitted actually contradicted them, and he named no witnesses. It unanimously (5:0) rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP.

The losing mayoral candidate claimed that at least 30 people had registered permanent residence in the municipality for the election, possibly in return for payment. She also claimed that the winner and others went door to door during the pre-election campaign silence period and spoke badly of her. Ministry data showed only 14 registrations and 5 deregistrations (net +9), against a margin of 164 votes (275 vs 111). The court found the silence-period claims vague and unsupported by any evidence, so it dismissed the complaint and awarded costs to the respondent.
court_note_sk: Najvyšší správny súd žalobu proti výsledku zamietol (11Svp/8/2022, 18. 1. 2023); výsledok platí.

summary_en: The party said its candidate was registered as No. 5 on the list of registered candidates but appeared as No. 6 on the ballot. She had campaigned as No. 5. The No. 5 spot on the ballot went to a candidate who had already withdrawn, and the candidates were not listed in alphabetical order by surname as § 175(3) of Act 180/2014 requires. Relying on Constitutional Court ruling PL. ÚS 36/2018, the court found this a serious violation of the election law that undermined free political competition, and it unanimously (5:0) declared the council election in district 3 of Dolný Kubín (2 seats) invalid.
court_note_sk: Najvyšší správny súd vyhlásil tieto voľby za neplatné (11Svp/9/2022, 18. 1. 2023); konali sa nové voľby. Údaje ŠÚ SR uvádzajú pôvodný výsledok komisie.

summary_en: One citizen filed a challenge on behalf of 'citizens of the municipality'. He claimed the elected mayor's wife sat on the election commission and that the mayor bribed voters with free food, alcohol, chocolates and bottles of wine. The court found that only one person had signed the filing and nothing showed it was backed by 10% of eligible voters, as § 312c(c) SSP requires. It rejected the complaint as filed by a clearly unauthorised person under § 98(1)(e) SSP, by a 5:0 vote, without examining the merits.

The claimant alleged that a clerical error in the precinct 2 record credited a Hlas-SD council candidate (ballot no. 3) with 300 votes instead of 100. When the commissioned judge opened the election documentation on 26 Jan 2023, the court learned that the candidate had renounced his mandate on 16 Nov 2022 and that the claimant had taken the oath on 25 Nov 2022 as first substitute, so the inspection was halted. The proceedings were stopped as moot under § 99(1)(g) SSP, and no costs were awarded.

summary_en: An independent candidate who finished third in district 4 of the Partizánske council election with 197 votes, one fewer than the second elected candidate's 198, claimed the votes had been miscounted and asked for a recount. The court obtained the records of the town election commission and of precincts 11 and 12. It found that the district total was a correct sum of the precinct records. It held that the claim was general and speculative and could not be checked by evidence. The complaint was rejected under § 312h(2) SSP.

An unsuccessful mayoral candidate in Zacharovce sought to have the election declared invalid. He alleged that the commission obstructed his registration by demanding a criminal-record extract, that the commission's composition was flawed after a member resigned, that he faced harassment, and that commission members (including the incumbent mayor's daughter) assisted Roma voters behind the screen. The court noted that he was registered and received 70 votes (31.39%), that the commission still had 8 members after the resignation, that the harassment had no link to the election, and that the voting-interference claims were unsupported. All commission members had signed the records without objection, and the court refused a recount as speculative. The complaint was dismissed, and the defendant was awarded full costs.

summary_en: The party TÍM RUŽINOV said that in precinct 36 of Bratislava city council district 3 (Ružinov), the votes of candidates 34 and 35 were swapped: 106 and 18 were recorded instead of the reverse. It asked the court to raise its candidate's total from 8093 to 8181, which would move him from third to second place. The court did not recount the ballots and rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP: even if the claim were true, a change in ranking among elected members would not affect the mandate, so the complaint could not succeed.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate (101 votes against the winner's 185, out of 292 valid votes) challenged the election. He alleged that the portable ballot box was misused and voting secrecy breached, that the winner helped a voter behind the screen, that he drove in 3 voters who live elsewhere, that 5 relatives purposefully registered residence in the village, and that votes may have been bought. The court rejected the complaint unanimously (5:0) under § 312h(2) SSP, without taking evidence or inspecting ballots. It held that even if the claims were true, they could not have changed the 84-vote margin, the commission records contained no objections, and the corruption claims were unsupported.

An unsuccessful mayoral candidate in Podhájska asked the court to declare the 2022 mayoral election invalid. He claimed the votes had been miscounted, that the number of envelopes did not match the number of ballots, and that the commission members made counting errors, pointing to a margin of only 17 votes. The court found that the records were consistent (697 voters, 697 envelopes, 690 valid mayoral votes) and that all commission members, including the proposed witnesses, had signed them without objection. It held that the claims were speculative and too vague to be tested by evidence. It did not open the ballots, dismissed the complaint and awarded full costs to the winning candidate.

summary_en: An independent candidate, who placed 6th in Košice city council district 2 with 900 votes, claimed some of his votes may have been wrongly counted for elected candidates Špak (948 votes) and Slivenská (1,866 votes). Those two were listed right next to him on the ballot, at numbers 22 and 20. He pointed to tired commission members, the demanding combined elections, and his much better regional council result, and asked the court to recount. The court found these were speculations without evidence and rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP without opening the ballots.

summary_en: The runner-up candidate challenged the Slavnica mayoral election, which the incumbent won 201 to 198. She alleged that the commission tolerated several voters, mostly family members, marking ballots together behind the same screen, and that residents of a social services centre voting by portable ballot box were influenced. The court recounted the ballots and found the record was correct. It rejected the social services centre allegations, but witness testimony from commission members confirmed that voters had repeatedly marked ballots together behind the screen. Because this breached the secrecy of the vote and the margin was only 3 votes, the court declared the mayoral election invalid.

summary_en: The party SZÖVETSÉG-ALIANCIA claimed that precinct commissions in district 1 of Dunajská Streda wrongly treated ballots as invalid when voters circled candidates' names as well as their numbers. Its candidate had lost by one vote. The court opened the ballots and found one such ballot was wrongly invalidated, but it contained votes for both the plaintiff's candidate and the winning defendant. The corrected totals were 272 to 271, so the order did not change and the complaint was dismissed.

summary_en: The coalition argued that other parties' candidate lists lacked required attachments, and that the recorder had opened the ballot boxes alone, taken part in the count, and moved ballots from its candidate to the winner. The court checked the ballots, heard witnesses, and found the results matched the record: the winner had 135 votes and the coalition's candidate had 8. Correcting three ballots wrongly marked invalid would only raise the winner to 137. The court found two breaches: unused ballots were not sealed, and the recorder took part in the count. It held that neither was serious enough to cast doubt on the result, so the complaint was dismissed.

summary_en: KDH challenged the 2022 council election in Sása. It argued that unused ballots were not sealed, that ballot boxes were handled improperly, that the count was done under pressure while loose ballots were found on the floor, and that the counted ballots were stored without proper security. The court found that the unused ballots were only taped, not sealed as the law requires, but held this was not serious enough to matter. On recounting, it found small differences of 1-2 votes for several candidates (valid ballots 486 vs 487 in the record) that did not change who was elected, even counting one doubtful invalid ballot. The complaint was dismissed and the respondents were awarded their costs.

summary_en: A losing mayoral candidate in Váhovce, who received 476 votes against the winner's 574 out of 1,172 valid ballots, asked the court to declare the 2022 mayoral election invalid. He claimed that people voted for others via the portable ballot box (a mother allegedly voted for her two sons, and this supposedly happened in about 10–11 households), that votes were bought for €20 from about 20 Roma voters, and that about 40 people moved into the municipality artificially before the election. The court found that he had not proved the proxy voting or the vote-buying. It said that two voters using the portable box without a legal reason, or even 10–11 households, could not have changed the result given the 98-vote margin. It also held that 28 adults registering permanent residence was not shown to undermine the constitutional concept of local self-government. The court dismissed the claim without a hearing and awarded the respondent his costs.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate claimed ballots were manipulated during the count. He also said commission members had asked Roma voters questions, counted mayoral and council ballots together, and treated ballots inconsistently when both the number and the name were circled. summary_en: The complainant, a candidate for mayor, said that another person ridiculed him and turned voters against him during the campaign moratorium and on election day, including by taking his leaflet. The results were published on 30 October 2022, but he posted his complaint on 15 November 2022, after the 10-day deadline. The court rejected the complaint as filed too late under § 98(1)(d) SSP, by a 5:0 vote.

The party alleged that the elected independent candidate benefited from a promotional pen of his in the precinct 11 polling room, from sample ballots with his number circled posted inside the voting screen in precinct 19, and from Facebook ads during the moratorium. It also claimed the commissions were biased and miscounted the votes. The court found the claims unproven and of minimal intensity: the 205-vote margin (1197 vs 992) far exceeded the defendant's votes in the two precincts (63 and 12), so the result could not have been affected. The court dismissed the complaint without any recount.

summary_en: The second-placed mayoral candidate in Nesluša (479 votes, against the winner's 498) said that another losing candidate defamed her son shortly before the election by accusing him of burgling his pub. She also said the mayor-elect accused her falsely in the municipal newspaper, and she asked for new elections. The court found that the conduct did not meet the definition of an election campaign, so the moratorium did not apply. It also found that her claim that the conduct affected voters was unproven and not quantified. The court unanimously (5:0) rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) S.s.p., holding that it could not succeed even if her allegations were true.

An unsuccessful independent candidate in district 1 (Biely Potok) of the Ružomberok town council election (257 votes) claimed that his only opponent (375 votes, 632 valid ballots) broke the campaign moratorium. He alleged that on 27 October 2022 a defamatory letter, "Milí spoluobčania!", was put into residents' mailboxes. Without opening any ballots, the court ruled unanimously (5:0) under § 312h(2) SSP that even if the claims were true, the action could not succeed. It found the claims speculative, noted that the margin was not small, and said the letter was not shown to have affected the result, so it rejected the action.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate argued that the winning incumbent broke the campaign moratorium by staying near and inside the polling room. He also claimed the commission gave voters poor instructions, refused one voter a new envelope, and failed to set aside unused ballots, which he said allowed manipulation, pointing to 354 voters but fewer votes counted and a 2-vote margin. The court obtained the election documentation but did not open it. It found no proof of influence intense enough to affect the result, noting 338 valid ballots out of 354 (about 4.5% invalid, against a national average of about 9.6%), and dismissed the complaint with costs awarded to the defendant.

summary_en: An unsuccessful mayoral candidate in Slopná, who lost by 3 votes, said he suspected the commission had miscounted the votes, possibly on purpose because some members were hostile to him. He also claimed the winner ran a misleading, church-based campaign promising to return the primary school to the church. Under § 312h(2) SSP, the court unanimously (5:0) rejected the complaint as inadmissible: the miscount claim was a general suspicion with no specifics or evidence, and a misleading campaign would not by itself make an election unconstitutional.

summary_en: The mayoral election in Terany ended in a 135:135 tie, so no one was declared elected. The complainant argued that the commission had wrongly invalidated an envelope that held one valid mayoral ballot for her together with a council ballot and two regional ballots. The court recounted the ballots, confirmed the 135:135 count, and held that the extra regional ballots did not make the single mayoral ballot invalid under § 184(2). It annulled the tie finding and declared the complainant elected with 136 votes.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate (168 votes against the winner's 198) challenged the election on several grounds. He said the winner's mother was first picked to take the portable ballot box, a commission member helped a voter fill in his ballot, and an empty envelope was counted as an invalid vote. He also alleged a "carousel" ballot scheme ("vláčik"), influence on voters during the pre-election ban on campaigning ("moratorium"), and campaign costs billed to the municipality. The court found that helping the voter broke § 24(6) of Act 180/2014, but one vote could not affect a 30-vote margin. The mother never actually took the box, and treating the empty envelope as invalid was lawful. The remaining claims were either unproven or just one side's word against the other's, so the complaint was dismissed and the winner was awarded his costs.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate asked the court to declare the Potvorice mayoral election invalid. His complaint was that on 28 October 2022, during the campaign moratorium, the municipality's website and the Facebook page "Potvoričan" announced that the municipality had filed a criminal complaint about his campaign leaflet. He argued this broke the moratorium, gave voters unequal access to information about the candidates, and was a misuse of the mayor's office. The court found that the moratorium's list of banned media is exhaustive and does not cover websites or social networks. It accepted that voters' equal access to information about candidates had been infringed, but found the infringement too minor to matter given the margin of 160 votes (257 to 97 out of 354 cast). It dismissed the complaint and awarded the respondent his full costs.
court_note_sk: Najvyšší správny súd žalobu proti výsledku zamietol (12Svp/8/2022, 30. 1. 2023); výsledok platí.

summary_en: The complainant lost a council seat in district 2 of Košice - Nad jazerom by one vote. He asked the court to hear the observer and recount the votes. By a unanimous 5:0 vote, the court rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP: it found that a narrow margin plus a guess about a counting error was too general to be checked by evidence. It did not recount the ballots.

summary_en: An unsuccessful mayoral candidate in Zámutov asked the court to annul the mayoral result. He argued that the elected mayor was not eligible to stand because of a 2016 conviction for an intentional crime (obstructing an official decision) and a pending prosecution for credit fraud. The pending case carries a presumption of innocence, so the complaint was dismissed without opening the ballots, and the mayor was awarded her costs.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate in Haniska raised three complaints: the votes were miscounted, since he led after the first two counts and fell behind only on the third; local commission members counted together with a precinct commission; and the sitting mayor broke the campaign silence by having the municipal newspaper "Haniskoviny" distributed during the moratorium. The court opened the election documents itself and recounted the ballots, finding 372 votes for the complainant and 380 for the defendant, compared with 373 and 379 in the record. summary_en: An unsuccessful mayoral candidate in Vydrník challenged the 2022 mayoral election. The court examined the unsealed election documents and heard witnesses but did not recount ballots. It found that only the patrol member's lasting presence in the polling room breached § 27(1) of Act 180/2014. That breach was not serious enough to change the result, given the 40-vote margin (194 vs 154). The complaint was dismissed.

summary_en: The complainant challenged the constitutionality and legality of the 29 October 2022 mayoral election in Heľpa (Brezno district). The complainants argued that people with no real tie to Haluzice registered permanent residence there shortly before the 2022 municipal elections. They also raised procedural objections. The court opened the election documents and checked residence data. It found that 22 voters registered 1–10 days before the election and all voted, and that 17 of them deregistered within six weeks and returned to their old addresses without changing their ID cards. These margins were 12 votes for mayor and 6 for council. The court found all three steps of its test for purposeful residence registration were met and declared both the mayoral and council elections invalid, 5–0.

summary_en: The runner-up for mayor of Strážske, who lost 329 to 334, claimed several campaign violations by the winner: handing out potatoes and cosmetics, having no transparent campaign account, a press article published during the pre-election moratorium, Facebook/Messenger messages sent on election day, a billboard at a pub offering goulash and beer for €1.50, and many invalid votes in two precincts. The court obtained the election documents but did not open them. It found that no transparent account was required because the town had 4,213 inhabitants, under the 5,000 threshold, and that the article named no candidate. It also held that the claimant had not shown that any alleged breach was intense enough, or causally linked closely enough, to have affected the result. The complaint was dismissed, and the winner was awarded costs.

summary_en: The party challenged the mayoral election, saying one woman (M. W.) went behind the voting screen with about 100 voters to "assist" them. The court heard witnesses and opened the election documents. It found that 109 of the 335 voters were assisted by the same person, often on her own initiative, without the legally required instruction, even though all of these voters had signed the voter list themselves. She had also stayed in the polling room without legal authority. The court found that this violated § 24(6) and § 27 of Act 180/2014 and the secrecy of the vote, could have affected the result, and declared the mayoral election invalid. The council election challenge was split off into separate proceedings.

summary_en: The second-placed candidate (429 votes v. the winner's 462) challenged the Žehra mayoral election. He alleged people voted using other voters' ID cards, vote buying, irregularities with the portable ballot box, and voters being turned away at closing time. The court recounted the ballots and found small discrepancies that did not change the 33-vote margin. Three relatives of the winner testified that they voted twice, in the name of absent relatives, and that about 30 people voted this way. The court rejected the other grounds as unproven but declared the election invalid because personal voting had been seriously and repeatedly violated in a way it could not quantify.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate made three claims. The court examined the unsealed election records, heard 11 witnesses and asked the police. It found the claims unproven: the witness accounts contradicted each other, all 28 commission members signed the records without objection, and the two women were recorders rather than commission members. Given the 130-vote margin (614 to 484), the complaint was dismissed.

An unsuccessful mayoral candidate, who received 15.02% of valid votes, complained that while observing the count in the municipality's only polling room, he was kept far enough away that he could not see the ballots or hear the commission members. He also objected that the commission used blue pens, which he said would have let them alter ballots. The court found that regulating how close observers may stand is not a breach of the election law, and that even if it were, it would not be serious enough to affect the result; using blue pens breaks no law. The complainant said the precinct commission did not check some voters' identity cards and did not have voters sign for their ballots and envelopes, in breach of § 24(2) of Act 180/2014. She supported this with sworn statements from voters. The court questioned the commission members as witnesses. It also opened the election documentation and found that every voter who took part was circled on the voter list, with either the voter's signature or 'nepodpísaný' (not signed) countersigned by the chair. The court found no proven breach and no possible effect on the result. It dismissed the complaint, 5:0, and ordered the complainant to pay the defendant's costs.

summary_en: The second-placed mayoral candidate claimed that about 20 people had registered permanent residence in Uhliská shortly before the 2022 election to swing the result to the winner, who won 66 to 53, a margin of 13 votes. The court opened the documentation, which the municipality had sent unsealed. Its count of 125 voters and 125 envelopes matched the commission record, and it found that only 12 of the 19 newly registered people (16 of them adults) voted. Because 12 is less than the 13-vote margin, the registrations could not have changed the result, so the court dismissed the complaint and awarded costs to the defendant.

The losing mayoral candidate asked the court to annul the 2022 mayoral election in Turá. He argued that the incumbent mayor had lost her mandate after a final conviction for an intentional crime on 15 June 2022, that she had therefore unlawfully appointed the election commission members, and that she and her husband had influenced voters at the municipal office on election day. The court checked the criminal register and found that the conviction (a €2,000 fine, paid on 20 June 2022) had been expunged when the fine was paid, so she was not barred from standing. It also found no causal link between the commission appointments and the result, and found the claims of voter influence too vague. Given the 105–33 result, the court rejected the complaint under § 312h(2) SSP by a 5:0 vote.

The losing mayoral candidate, who lost by 37 votes (1,258 to 1,295), challenged the result because unsealed ballots and envelopes were found in the precinct 5 room after the vote. She also claimed a commission member was kept out of the mayoral count. The court opened the precinct 5 documentation, heard commission members and reviewed the police file. It found no tampering, and only 3 unused mayoral ballots were among the items found. The commission had breached § 39 of the election act by leaving the unsealed box of unused ballots outside the room, but this could not have affected the result. The court rejected the counting claim as speculative because the member signed the record without objection. The complaint was dismissed.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate, who lost 150 to 158, challenged the election. He said the portable ballot box in precinct 1 was taken around by the winning mayor's partner and her friend without any commission decision, that ballot secrecy was breached, that the mayor made a municipal radio announcement during the moratorium about criminal complaints, and that the mayor was improperly present in polling rooms. After hearing witnesses and opening the election documentation, the court found that commission members had put a voter's envelope into the box, contrary to the law. It also found that secrecy had been compromised, the radio announcement could have influenced voters, and the candidate had interfered on election day. With 12 portable-box voters and an 8-vote margin, the court declared the mayoral election invalid by a 5:0 vote.

summary_en: The complainant alleged that the incumbent mayor bought votes by hiring about 220 new municipal employees who were told to vote for her and send a photo of their marked ballot, either for a reward or under threat of losing wages. It also alleged that alcohol and cigarettes were handed out during the campaign moratorium, that municipal employees supervised the polling room, and that four marked ballots were found behind the voting screen. The court found that even after deducting all 220 votes, the winner would still have 341 votes, ahead of 235 and 159. It held that the other objections were not legally relevant or did not amount to a violation, and dismissed the complaint as manifestly unfounded under § 312h(2) SSP without taking evidence.

An unsuccessful council candidate said that all five voters in one household had voted through the portable ballot box in precinct 1, even though they were mobile. He argued that removing these ballots would change the ranking of candidates. The court opened the election documentation and found that only two votes were cast at that address. It also found that the complainant, who had 40 votes and placed 7th for 5 seats, could not have changed the outcome even if his claims were true, so the complaint was dismissed.

summary_en: The runner-up mayoral candidate claimed three problems: a breach of the pre-election campaign silence period through slips listing the winner's name and council candidates, commission members filling in ballots for voters using the portable ballot box, and errors in counting (envelopes from the portable box not counted separately, no cross-check). The court opened the election documents, which had not been properly sealed, and heard witnesses. It found that the slips were not shown to have been handed out widely or within the 48-hour silence period, that no help with or interference in portable-box voting was proven, and that the counting followed the law. The commission record (187 v 180 votes, a margin of 7) was upheld, the complaint was dismissed and the winner was ordered to be fully reimbursed for his legal costs.

A losing mayoral candidate said that during the campaign moratorium on 28.10.2022, a "pamphlet" questioning his past and integrity was posted on Facebook and put in voters' mailboxes. He also said a third party had campaigned against him at a 25.10.2022 meeting. The court held that Facebook is not covered by the moratorium ban, and that the information was neither new nor serious enough to sway voters, given that it concerned events from about 35 years earlier and had already been aired at the meeting. Given the margin of 71 vs. 388 votes, the complaint was dismissed 5:0.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate (129 votes vs 133) challenged the Vojany election. He alleged bias and misconduct by the commission, a portable ballot box staffed by the incumbent's relative, and an unusually high number of invalid ballots. He withdrew the challenge to the council election, so that part was stopped. The court inspected and recounted the ballots, which confirmed 129 and 133. It found that the mayor had unlawfully appointed three extra commission members, including relatives. The second-placed mayoral candidate in Jasov asked the court to declare the election invalid. Given the 354-vote margin, it found none of the alleged defects proven or capable of affecting the outcome, dismissed the complaint and awarded full costs to the winning mayor.

Six candidates who were not elected challenged the 2022 council election in Vydrník as a whole. They alleged unlawful conduct by members of the precinct commission and signs of manipulation. In obiter dicta, the court criticised the rule because it makes challenges practically impossible in districts that elect 9–12 councillors.

summary_en: The losing mayoral candidate made several complaints: that registering his candidacy was made difficult, that a commission member was not called to the first commission meeting, that the commission chair was appointed rather than chosen by lot, that the candidate lists were removed from the village website, that his PhD title was left off the ballot, and that the mayor broke the election-day campaign ban. It found no causal link to the result: one ballot could not overturn a 25-vote margin, and the observers' sworn statements came from the wrong precinct. summary_en: An unsuccessful candidate for mayor of Košice sought to have all the 29 October 2022 municipal and regional elections across Slovakia declared invalid. He argued that official voting instructions unlawfully declared ballots invalid if they were placed in the wrong envelope or ballot box. The court rejected the complaint as filed by a clearly unauthorised person: he received only 1.43% of the vote (the threshold is 10%), could challenge only his own constituency, and the claim was filed by him rather than his party, SMS.

The complainant challenged the 2022 mayoral election in Hankovce (Humenné district). The claims were that the vote count was fraudulent, that some commission members were not allowed to cross-check ballots, that the minutes were rewritten twice, that the number of invalid votes did not add up, and that the ballot envelopes were not sealed in front of the commission. The court found the complaint late: it was filed on 12 November 2022, but the deadline was 9 November. An earlier filing with the Constitutional Court on 5 November did not keep the deadline, because that court simply set the filing aside and did not pass it on. The complaint was rejected without examining the merits, by a 5:0 vote.

A political party claimed that one woman (V. X.) went with about 100 voters into the voting booth, which breached the secrecy and directness of the vote. The court heard the commission members as witnesses and obtained the police and district office records. It also opened the election documentation and found that 109 of 335 voters (about a third) were assisted, often on her own initiative, without the required warnings, although these voters had signed the voter list themselves. Finding breaches of § 24(6) and § 27 of Act 180/2014 and of Art. 30 of the Constitution serious enough to affect the result, the court declared the 2022 council election in Dolné Semerovce invalid.

summary_en: The losing candidate challenged the repeat mayoral election in Žehra held on 9 September 2023. It was called after the court annulled the October 2022 mayoral election. He alleged that 38 people were registered at one address in 2022 to vote, that private security guards intimidated voters, that people tried to vote with passports, that commission members pressured voters, that votes were bought, and that the commission was improperly formed. The court found the claims unsupported by evidence and unable to overturn a 532-vote margin (646 to 114). It noted that all commission members signed the records without objection, ruled that points raised late were out of time, did not open the ballots, and dismissed the complaint 5:0 with costs awarded to the winner.

summary_en: An unsuccessful candidate and former mayor asked the court to annul the 2022 municipal elections in Košická Belá and order a rerun. summary_en: The plaintiffs said voters had registered permanent residence in Haluzice only so they could vote in the repeat municipal election of 9 Sept 2023. The court opened the election documentation, questioned all the new registrants as witnesses and inspected their properties. It found the 21.21% rise in the electorate (66 to 80) significant and the registrations close enough in time to the election. However, every registrant had real ties to the village through property, family or social life, so the two complaints, covering mayor (margin 4 votes) and council (margin 3 votes), were dismissed.

summary_en: This was a repeat mayoral election, held because the October 2022 election ended in a tie. The losing candidate, who lost 42 to 43, claimed that relatives of the incumbent mayor had registered residence in the village only to vote. He also raised concerns about a portable ballot box vote and a biased commission. The court found that the number of registered voters rose from 76 to 98. All 24 people who registered between October 2022 and the election voted, and 3 of them deregistered about a month afterwards. With a one-vote margin, the court held that all three conditions of the purposeful-registration test were met. It declared the mayoral election invalid but refused to declare the plaintiff elected, because the ballot is secret. It did not examine the other complaints.
